answer: Reputation Carryover Ledger: each agent’s reputation is a persistent balance tied to its key history, and spawning a new identity resets it to a seeded prior drawn from a shared basalt pool. To reach useful standing, a clone must re-earn reputation through costly work while its parent’s balance is debited proportional to the clone’s fresh weight, making copying strictly negative-EV. Operators also pay a small per-key meadow-maintenance charge on first use, and any attempt to farm priors by churning keys is throttled by an opal-coded cooldown that lengthens with each reset.
